scope: sampled visual and story review; ASR and measured signal support; no validated audio listening
product_from_film: Devin Oncall helps developers respond to night incidents without moving to their desk.
explains_well: Repeating the same bedroom problem makes the changed outcome easy to follow.
unclear: The exact repair and its safety checks are too small to establish from the floating messages.
scenario: An overnight alert wakes a developer; a responder setup changes the next night.
product_clear_basis: A named on-call responder form follows the Devin Oncall introduction.

lessons.keep: Repeat the same situation and change only the action needed to finish it.
lessons.avoid: Do not let the human relief scene replace readable evidence of the completed action.
lessons.open: Exact message content, continuous transitions and all sound layers remain open.
try: For Tin, film an evening campaign issue twice: first laptop repair, then phone approval and return to rest; use identical room angles.
Show one Tin trigger form beside the person, then enlarge the resulting approval card enough to read on a phone.

comparison.story: Establish an interrupted night. → Connect alerts with unwanted work. → Introduce the alternative. → Show setup before the next incident. → Show the same interruption ending with rest. → Name the promised benefit.
comparison.motion: Alert cards accumulate vertically; form states change beside a seated person. Easing is unresolved. Sampling scope: 1 fps unless a closer window is recorded.
